newsitem.title: GERMANY: German television network Sat1 sees March recovery.
newsitem.headline: German television network Sat1 sees March recovery.

text.p: After suffering blows to its market share and advertising income in the last two months, German television network Sat1 said its initial March results showed it was on the road to recovery.
The private broadcaster has pumped up its market share by two percent to just under 15 percent of viewers, which the station said was above expectations.
"We lost shares in 1996 due to programming changes," a Sat1 spokewoman said on Tuesday. "We've been through a slump. But it looks as though something has given way."

She said pushing back prime-time programmes to 8:15 p.m., which stops them conflicting with the popular 8 p.m. nightly news, in-house programme development, new crime shows and Sunday soccer broadcasts had all helped boost Sat1's ratings.
But media agencies, responsible for selling media advertising time, and industry observers said it would take a while before Sat1 was in the black for the first time.

"I do not think Sat1 is having serious crises, but it has also not had very positive development," said Hartmut Scheiber, electronic media director for HMS Carat, Germany's largest media sales agency.

He added that media agencies were pleased Sat1 had lowered its advertising prices in response to lower demand, but that this scaling back had as a result undermined their advertising placement strategy.
Industry representatives were also sceptical about the station's prognosis, in part due to spats between primary shareholders -- media group Kirch and publishing company Axel Springer Verlag AG.
Kirch announced in January it planned to acquire publishing group Georg von Holtzbrinck's and media company Ravensburger Film + TV GmbH's shares in Sat1, sparking conflict with Axel Springer Verlag.
